# Bynk

> Bynk is a statically typed, architecture-first programming language for building
> services. The shape of a program — its contexts, services, agents, and the types
> that flow between them — is part of the language, not a convention layered on top.
> Bynk compiles to typed TypeScript and targets Cloudflare Workers. It is pre-1.0
> and evolves in small, spec-first increments (currently v0.476).

This file is a self-contained primer for an LLM agent. The first half teaches
enough Bynk to read and write it; the second half links to the canonical [Bynk
Book](/book/) for depth. When in doubt, the Book documents *what compiles today*;
features marked "planned" are deferred, not available. Every `bynk` code block
below is compiled (or, when marked `fragment`, parsed) by the toolchain's CI, so
the syntax shown is current. The whole Book as one file is at `/llms-full.txt`.

Bynk is young, so your training data may hold older syntax. Before you write
Bynk, prefer this file and the Book over memory; after you write it, run
`bynk check`. `bynk explain <code>` explains any diagnostic code.

## Core ideas

- **Make illegal states unrepresentable.** Refined types (a base type carrying a
  predicate), opaque types, and errors-as-values (`Result`, `Option`) keep whole
  classes of bug unexpressed.
- **Architecture is in the language.** `context`, `service`, and stateful `agent`
  are first-class. A `context` is the unit of deployment — it compiles to one
  Cloudflare Worker.
- **Honest effects and capabilities.** Side effects have type `Effect[T]`.
  Dependencies are declared in signatures with `given`, supplied by the platform
  or a `provides` block, and replaced by `stub`s in tests.
- **Compiles to readable, typed TypeScript.** The router, boundary validation, and
  Worker entry point are generated for you.
- **Testing is built in.** `suite` and `case` blocks, `expect`, `stub` test
  doubles, `Val[T]` value fabrication, generative `property` tests, and three
  tiers (`unit`, `integration`, `system`) ship with the language.

## File and project shape

- Source files use the `.bynk` extension and begin with `context <name>` (or
  `commons <name>` for a pure, stateless module). Dotted names like
  `context hello.web` are allowed.
- A project has a `bynk.toml` manifest, a `src/` directory, and a `tests/`
  directory for `suite` files. `bynk new <name>` scaffolds one; `bynk dev`
  compiles and serves it locally on `http://localhost:8787`.
- `//` begins a line comment. `--` is **not** a comment (it is two minus
  operators); `bynk fmt` rewrites the old `--` spelling.
- `---` … `---` (on their own lines) is a doc-block — Markdown attached to the
  following declaration — and `--- text` is a one-line doc.
- `uses <commons>` brings a commons module's types and functions into scope.
- `consumes bynk { Clock, Logger, Fetch }` imports first-party platform
  capabilities; `consumes bynk.cloudflare { Kv }` pins the context to Cloudflare.
- `consumes <context>` depends on another context's exported services, and
  `exports transparent { … }` / `exports opaque { … }` declare what a context
  exposes.

## Language tour (by example)

A minimal service:

```bynk
context greet

service api from http {
  on GET("/ping") () -> Effect[HttpResult[String]] by v: Visitor {
    Ok("pong")
  }
}
```

### Types

```bynk
type UserId = String where NonEmpty                  // refined: base type + predicate
type Title  = String where NonEmpty && MaxLength(200)
type Qty    = Int where Positive

type Order = { id: String, customer: String }        // record
type TodoError = enum { NotFound }                   // payloadless sum type
type Token = opaque String                           // opaque: nominally distinct, structure hidden
```

- A refined type's constructor is `T.of(value) -> Result[T, ValidationError]`. At
  a service boundary, route params and request bodies are validated through `.of`
  automatically (HTTP 400 on failure). An opaque type is built with `T.of(v)`
  or the unchecked `T.unsafe(v)`, only inside the unit that declares it.
- Records are constructed `Order { id: id, customer: c }` and updated functionally
  `Order { ...o, customer: c }`.
- Base types: `String`, `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, `Bytes`, `Duration` (ms, e.g.
  `5.minutes`), `Instant` (epoch ms, from `Clock.now()` or
  `Instant.fromEpochMillis(n)`). Library types: `Option[T]`, `Result[T, E]`,
  `Effect[T]`, `List[T]`, `Map[K, V]`.

### Errors and optionals as values

```bynk,fragment
match Title.of(name) {
  Ok(title) => Ok(greeting(title))
  Err(_)    => BadRequest("name must be non-empty and at most 200 characters")
}
```

```bynk,fragment
match found {                 // found : Option[Item]
  Some(it) => Ok(it)
  None     => NotFound
}
```

- `Result[T, E]` has variants `Ok(T)` / `Err(E)`. `Option[T]` has `Some(T)` / `None`.
- `match` is exhaustive. `is` tests a value against a variant pattern, yielding a
  `Bool` (e.g. `if (mo is None) { 1 } else { 0 }`).
- `let Ok(x) = r else { … }` binds on a match and runs the `else` block otherwise.
- `Json.decode[T](s) -> Result[T, JsonError]` and `Json.encode(v) -> String`.

### Effects and capabilities

Effectful work has type `Effect[T]`. Inside a handler, `let x <- expr` sequences
an effect (binds its result); `let x = expr` binds a pure value; `do expr` runs a
unit effect as a statement. `par { let a <- e1  let b <- e2 }` issues independent
effects together and waits for all of them; it holds only `let x <- e` and `do e`,
no binding may mention a sibling's name, and a fault raises the first in source
order once every effect has settled. `e.within(d)` bounds an effect's time and
yields `Result[T, TimedOut]` (`TimedOut` is `bynk`'s), in a service handler only; the
effect is not cancelled but handed to `waitUntil`, and may still complete. `a.race(b)` takes the first of two effects to succeed and hands the other to `waitUntil` to finish, so it is for idempotent work. `Effect.pure(v)` lifts a value. A handler declares
the capabilities it needs with `given`:

```bynk
context greeter

consumes bynk { Clock, Logger }

capability Rates {                   // your own capability: signatures, no bodies
  fn lookup(currency: String) -> Effect[Float]
}

provides Rates = FixedRates {        // one provider per capability in a context
  fn lookup(currency: String) -> Effect[Float] {
    Effect.pure(1.0)
  }
}

service api from http {
  on GET("/now") () -> Effect[HttpResult[String]] by v: Visitor given Clock, Logger, Rates {
    let t <- Clock.now()
    let rate <- Rates.lookup("GBP")
    do Logger.info("checked the clock")
    Ok("\(t.toEpochMillis()) at \(rate)")
  }
}
```

- First-party capabilities (`bynk`): `Clock`, `Random`, `Logger`, `Fetch`,
  `Secrets`, `Locale`, `Idempotency`, `Events`. Cloudflare-specific ones live in
  `bynk.cloudflare` (for example `Kv`, `R2`, `RateLimit`, `EdgeCache`).
- Calling a capability that is not in `given` is an error; a `given` that is
  never used is a warning.
- `"\(expr)"` is string interpolation.

### Agents (stateful, keyed)

An `agent` is a keyed, stateful unit — one instance per key, compiling to a
Cloudflare Durable Object. State lives in `store` fields; `on call` handlers are
its methods, invoked as `AgentName(key).method(args)`.

```bynk
context todos

type UserId = String where NonEmpty
type Title  = String where NonEmpty && MaxLength(200)

type TodoItem = { id: String, seq: Int, title: Title, done: Bool }

agent Todos {
  key owner: UserId                       // the address; one instance per distinct key

  store items:   Map[String, TodoItem]    // storage-backed collections
  store lastSeq: Cell[Int]                // a single mutable cell

  on call add(title: Title) -> Effect[TodoItem] {
    let next = lastSeq + 1
    let item = TodoItem { id: "\(next)", seq: next, title: title, done: false }
    let _ <- items.put(item.id, item)
    lastSeq := next                        // `:=` writes a store field
    item
  }

  on call pending() -> Effect[List[TodoItem]] {
    items.values.filter((it) => it.done == false).sortBy((it) => it.seq).collect()
  }
}
```

- Storage kinds: `Map[K, V]`, `Cell[T]`, `Cache[K, V]` (TTL-expiring, via
  `@ttl(30.minutes)`, and needs `given Clock`). `Map` fields can be
  `@indexed(by: field)` for indexed equality filters.
- Reads are lazy `Query[T]` values over `items.values`, `items.keys` or
  `items.entries`: `filter`, `map`, `sortBy`, `groupBy`, `joinOn`, `leftJoin`,
  then a terminal `collect()` / `count()` / `sum(...)`.
- `invariant` declares a predicate that must hold of every committed state
  (runtime-checked); `transition` constrains each step over `old`/`new` state;
  `implies` is logical implication.
- A stored record whose shape changes takes a `migrate from <n> (old: T) { … }`
  step; `bynk migrate` reports and sweeps stored state.
- `self` refers to the current instance inside a handler.

### Entry points (service protocols)

A `service X from <protocol>` groups handlers. Protocols are a closed set:
`http`, `cron`, `queue("name")`, `websocket(in: …, out: …)`, and
`Events(E)` for subscribers. A service with no `from` is an internal `call`
service.

```bynk
context shop

type Job = { orderId: String }

service api from http {
  on GET("/orders/:id") (id: String) -> Effect[HttpResult[String]] by v: Visitor {
    Ok(id)
  }
}

service checks from cron {
  on schedule("*/5 * * * *") (at: Int) -> Effect[Result[(), String]] {
    Ok(())
  }
}

service worker from queue("orders") {
  on message(message: Job) -> Effect[QueueResult] {
    Ack
  }
}
```

- HTTP result constructors map to status codes: `Ok` (200), `Created` (201),
  `NoContent` (204), `BadRequest`, `NotFound`, `ServerError`, and more. The
  handler return type is `Effect[HttpResult[T]]`.
- Cron has no ambient clock — the scheduled time `at` is passed in.
- A queue handler returns `Effect[QueueResult]`: `Ack`, or `Retry(reason)`.
- A `websocket` service has exactly one `on open` (which must name its actor with
  `by` and transfer the connection it receives into an agent), plus `on message`
  and `on close`.
- `event Name = { … }` declares a typed fact a context may emit with
  `Events.emit(e)`; another context subscribes with
  `service OnX from Events(Name) { on event(e: Name) -> Effect[()] { … } }`.

### Actors and access control

A handler names the actor it serves with `by`. `Visitor` is the built-in
anonymous public actor; a declared `actor` is an authenticated boundary contract:

```bynk
context todos.web

type UserId = String where NonEmpty

actor User { auth = Bearer(secret = "AUTH_JWT_SECRET"), identity = UserId }

service api from http {
  on GET("/me") () -> Effect[HttpResult[UserId]] by u: User {
    Ok(u.identity)                         // the verified, sealed UserId
  }
}
```

The verified identity is *sealed* — minted at the boundary, never forged
downstream — and is commonly used as an agent key so each caller gets private state.

### Testing

Tests live in `tests/`, in a `suite` naming the unit under test. Each `case`
checks its claims with `expect`:

```bynk,fragment
suite window

case "an over-limit request is denied" {
  let d = decide(0, 10, 5000, 60000, 10)
  expect d.allowed == false
  expect d.count == 10
}
```

- A case drives a service by its natural surface: `api.GET("/path") by Visitor`,
  `svc.call(args)`, `svc.schedule("…")`, `svc.message(m)`, `svc.event(e)`.
- `stub Cap.op(args) returns v` (or `fails`; `returns v after d` and `never` take virtual time, to test `e.within(d)` and `a.race(b)`) replaces a capability operation for
  a suite or a case; `advance Clock by 15.minutes` moves the test clock.
- `case "…" as integration` runs real collaborators within one context;
  `as system` stands contexts up as the Workers they deploy as and crosses the
  real wire. `unit` is the default and is never written.
- `property "…" { for all x: T … }` is a generative test; `Val[T]` fabricates
  values.
- `requires` / `ensures` declare function pre- and postconditions.

## Keywords

**60** hard keywords — never usable as an identifier:
`Bool` `Bytes` `Duration` `Effect` `Err` `Float` `Instant` `Int` `JsonError`
`None` `Ok` `Option` `Result` `Some` `String` `ValidationError` `actor`
`adapter` `agent` `as` `binding` `by` `capability` `commons` `consumes`
`context` `cron` `do` `else` `ensures` `enum` `expect` `exports` `false` `fn`
`from` `given` `http` `if` `implies` `invariant` `is` `let` `match` `opaque`
`property` `protocol` `provides` `queue` `record` `requires` `self` `service`
`stub` `transition` `transparent` `true` `type` `uses` `where`.

Reserved only in their own position (ordinary names elsewhere): `asset` `case`
`const` `embed` `event` `messages` `on` `suite`.

Contextual words (keywords in one place only): `advance` `derives` `drop` `key` `migrate`
`par` `private` `removed` `replaces` `store`.

Built-in type names, reserved in type position: `Asset` `BoundaryRejection`
`Connection` `History` `HttpResult` `List` `Map` `Query` `QueueResult`
`RequestHeaders` `Set` `Stream` `TokenClaims`.

## CLI

- `bynk new <name>` — scaffold a project (no toolchain needed, writes files only).
- `bynk check` · `bynk fmt` · `bynk test` — type-check, format, and run tests.
- `bynk explain <code>` — explain a diagnostic code, with an example and a Book link.
- `bynk dev` — compile and serve locally. `bynk deploy` — deploy to Cloudflare.
  `bynk doctor` — check the environment.
- `bynk add <package>` · `bynk fetch` · `bynk publish` — dependencies and the registry.
- `bynkc` (`compile`, `check`, `fmt`, `test`) is the pure-pipeline compiler for CI.
- `bynkc-lsp` — the language server (diagnostics, hover, completion,
  navigation, refactorings).
